title: AWX
description: AWX is the hands: every verb in infra-objectives executes through it. These are AWX's own metrics, scraped from OUTSIDE the cluster it runs in, so an outage shows as up == 0 rather than as missing data.

panels.title: AWX reachable
panels.description: The scrape runs from the PostgreSQL VM, outside the Kubernetes cluster AWX lives in. A 0 here is a measurement; if this panel is empty instead, the collector or Grafana is the problem, not AWX.

panels.title: Capacity remaining
panels.description: Summed across AWX instances. Jobs queue when this reaches zero — which looks like AWX being slow rather than AWX being full, and is the distinction this panel exists to make.

panels.title: Connection utilisation
panels.description: Backends in use as a percentage of the slots AWX may occupy (max_connections minus superuser_reserved_connections). Read from PostgreSQL directly by postgres_exporter, NOT from AWX. That distinction is the point: awx_database_connections_total comes from AWX, so when AWX cannot get a connection the metric goes to 'no data' rather than to red — it disappears exactly when it matters. This one keeps reporting while AWX is down. Both halves are metrics, so raising max_connections re-scales this automatically instead of leaving the panel grading against a stale number.

panels.title: Connection headroom
panels.description: Free slots before PostgreSQL starts refusing AWX. Derived entirely from metrics — no ceiling written into this dashboard. Read from PostgreSQL directly by postgres_exporter, NOT from AWX. That distinction is the point: awx_database_connections_total comes from AWX, so when AWX cannot get a connection the metric goes to 'no data' rather than to red — it disappears exactly when it matters. This one keeps reporting while AWX is down. Connections are held mostly by wsrelay, which meshes between awx-task pods, so headroom shrinks with the SQUARE of task_replicas.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: AWX control pods reporting capacity. south runs six; a drop means pods are gone or not heartbeating.

panels.title: Capacity per instance
panels.description: Per AWX pod. Pods come and go on redeploy, so gaps here are normal; all of them dropping at once is not.

panels.title: Connections vs the limit
panels.description: A climbing floor rather than a spike is the shape that precedes AWX becoming unusable. The limit line is read from pg_settings, so it moves when the setting moves. Read from PostgreSQL directly by postgres_exporter, NOT from AWX. That distinction is the point: awx_database_connections_total comes from AWX, so when AWX cannot get a connection the metric goes to 'no data' rather than to red — it disappears exactly when it matters. This one keeps reporting while AWX is down.

panels.title: Inventory of the estate, as AWX sees it
panels.description: Counts of the things this repo manages. Useful as a change detector: hosts or job templates moving when nobody deployed anything is worth a look.

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot tell you

options.content:
**PostgreSQL is now measured directly** (`postgres_exporter` via Alloy, peer auth over the unix socket, `pg_monitor` read-only). The connection panels no longer depend on AWX being able to answer, and no ceiling is hardcoded — `pg_settings_max_connections` is itself a metric, so the panels re-scale when the limit changes.

**On 2026-08-23 AWX sat at 95 of 97 usable connections** and PostgreSQL refused the rest with *remaining connection slots are reserved*. Not load: 91 idle, 1 active. 59 belonged to `wsrelay`, which meshes between `awx-task` pods, so the count grows with the square of `task_replicas` (6, in `helm-override-files/awx/awx.yml`).

**A connection pooler cannot fix it.** PgBouncer transaction mode — the only mode that reduces connections — breaks LISTEN/NOTIFY (13 backends hold channels) and session advisory locks (`pg_advisory_unlock`, on 14). The advisory-lock break is silent: the unlock lands on a different backend and the lock leaks. Session mode is 1:1 and saves nothing. Protocol-level, so pgcat and Odyssey inherit it.

---

**Nothing about AWX's pods.** These are AWX's own application metrics, reported by AWX about itself. Pod restarts, evictions, image pulls and scheduling failures need `kube-state-metrics`, which must run inside the cluster — blocked on the `infra-observability` ServiceAccount.

**Nothing about PostgreSQL itself.** `awx_database_connections_total` is AWX's view of its database. Disk, bloat, locks and replication need `postgres_exporter` and a read-only `pg_monitor` role on that VM.

**Nothing when AWX is down.** If AWX cannot serve `/api/v2/metrics`, every panel here goes flat except `up`, which is precisely why the scrape runs from outside the cluster. Cross-check with the **Management plane** dashboard: if the PostgreSQL VM and the Kubernetes nodes are healthy while AWX is not, the fault is in the application layer.

**Nothing about whether a job did the right thing.** AWX reports that jobs ran, not that they were correct — a job template pointed at an empty inventory reports success. See rule 8 in `CLAUDE.md`.
